art.title: A View on a High Road
art.why: No crossroads or signpost at NGA; a road winding into the distance with travellers resting and walking, for the question of which way. Describe only the one road the gallery describes; don't call it a crossroads.
No synagogue or rabbi in the NGA open-access paintings (searched synagogue, rabbi, Jew, Hebrew).

art.title: The Annunciation
art.why: The angel and Mary: the scene told in Sura 19 and Sura 3 as in Luke. The gallery reads Isaiah 7:14 in her book ('virgo concipiet'), which gives the lecture a way into what Christians and Muslims share and don't.
No Indian, Chinese or other Asian landscape among the open-access paintings (only a Qing 'Archery Contest' and a Rembrandt 'Man in Oriental Costume', neither fits).
No elephant in any NGA open-access painting title or description.

art.title: Scenes from the Passion of Christ: The Descent into Limbo [right panel]
art.why: Christ breaking the gates and taking an old man by the hand, a crowd waiting in the cave: the Harrowing of Hell, for 1 Peter 3:19. benvenuto-limbo is already used, so this is another.

art.title: Saint Francis [far left panel]
art.why: Francis standing with a book, in the rope-tied brown habit, for Francis who went to the Sultan. The description doesn't name him; the title does.
